- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment runs — adjust upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment shifts — lag corrections by 2–3 days unless sentiment is extreme.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative, forecast should trend toward historical mean over 10–14 day window.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% above recent high) should be capped at +3–5% of prior peak.
- If sentiment is consistently low (0.0–0.3) and price is trending down, forecast should not dip below 10% below recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid overfitting to recent 7–14 day highs — use 30-day moving average as baseline anchor.
